fullPassage: Plants are photosynthetic organisms that can create their own nourishment by using solar energy and minerals from the soil. Why, then, do some species of plants trap and seemingly eat insects and tiny animals like frogs? It is because they usually grow in nutrient-deficient habitats —like bogs— in which the soil is too acidic to provide necessary elements. Due to the environmental factors, over many successive generations, these plants have evolved unique mechanisms, such as pitcher-like bodies filled with sticky secretions or closing leaves, that trap animals. They have also gained enzymes that enable them to break down the food they consume and convert it into energy. As the enzymes work, they liquefy the prey’s body, releasing many of the nutrients that are absent from the soil. By absorbing this slurry, the plants get the nutrition they need to thrive in their ecosystem.

questions.passage: Plants are photosynthetic organisms that can create their own nourishment by using solar energy and minerals from the soil. Why, then, do some species of plants trap and <u>seemingly eat</u> insects and tiny animals like frogs? It is because they usually grow in nutrient-deficient habitats —like bogs— in which the soil is too acidic to provide necessary elements. Due to the environmental factors, over many successive generations, these plants have evolved unique mechanisms, such as pitcher-like bodies filled with sticky secretions or closing leaves, that trap animals. They have also gained enzymes that enable them to break down the food they consume and convert it into energy. As the enzymes work, they liquefy the prey’s body, releasing many of the nutrients that are absent from the soil. By absorbing this slurry, the plants get the nutrition they need to thrive in their ecosystem.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: '겉보기에 먹는다(seemingly eat)'는, 진짜 포식이 아니라 척박한 토양에서 부족한 양분을 보충하려는 적응 행동이라는 뜻이에요.
det.analysis:
밑줄 뒤 글 전체가 '양분이 부족한 환경 때문에' 동물을 잡는다고 설명하는 게 단서예요.

① 완전히 소화해 영구 저장한다는 과장된 해석이에요

② 곤충을 잡는 기관을 진화시켰으니 관심이 없다는 건 반대예요

③ 먹는 것처럼 보이지만 실제로는 부족한 양분을 얻으려는 적응이라는 뜻 — 밑줄의 함의를 정확히 담아요 ←정답

④ 곤충이 식물을 공격하는 게 아니라 식물이 곤충을 잡아요
det.tip: seemingly eat → 포식이 아니라 양분 보충 적응.

ch: 곤충을 완전히 소화해 몸속에 영구히 저장한다는 뜻
곤충을 잡는 일에는 전혀 관심이 없다는 뜻
먹는 것처럼 보이지만 사실 부족한 양분을 얻으려는 적응이라는 뜻
곤충이 오히려 식물을 공격해 먹어 치운다는 뜻

Due to the environmental factors, over many successive generations, these plants have evolved unique mechanisms, such as pitcher-like bodies filled with sticky secretions or closing leaves, that trap animals. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 them이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밑줄 친 them은 앞 문장의 주어 '이 식물들(these plants = They)'을 가리켜요.
det.analysis:
밑줄 앞 'They have also gained enzymes that enable them to break down the food(그들은 먹이를 분해하게 해 주는 효소를 얻었다)'가 단서예요. 효소 덕분에 분해할 수 있게 된 주체는 식물이에요.

① 효소들 — 효소는 them이 분해하도록 '돕는' 도구라 지칭 대상이 아니에요

② 식충 식물들 — 효소를 얻어 먹이를 분해하게 된 주체라 them이 가리키는 대상이에요 ←정답

③ 곤충들 — 곤충은 분해되는 먹이라 주체가 아니에요

④ 토양 속 무기질들 — 문맥상 지칭 대상이 아니에요
det.tip: They(=plants) gained enzymes that enable them → 식물들.

questions.passage: Plants are photosynthetic organisms that can create their own nourishment by using solar energy and minerals from the soil. Why, then, do some species of plants trap and seemingly eat insects and tiny animals like frogs? It is because they usually grow in nutrient-deficient habitats —like bogs— in which the soil is too acidic to provide necessary elements. Due to the environmental factors, over many successive generations, these plants have evolved unique mechanisms, such as pitcher-like bodies filled with sticky secretions or closing leaves, that __________. They have also gained enzymes that enable them to break down the food they consume and convert it into energy. As the enzymes work, they liquefy the prey’s body, releasing many of the nutrients that are absent from the soil. By absorbing this slurry, the plants get the nutrition they need to thrive in their ecosystem.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: trap animals=동물을 가두다 / produce bright flowers=화려한 꽃을 피우다 / store extra rainwater=여분의 빗물을 저장하다 / reflect strong sunlight=강한 햇빛을 반사하다
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞 'unique mechanisms, such as pitcher-like bodies filled with sticky secretions or closing leaves, that ______(끈끈한 분비물로 찬 주머니 모양 몸체나 닫히는 잎 같은, ______하는 독특한 기관)'가 단서예요. 끈끈한 분비물과 닫히는 잎의 목적이에요.

① trap animals: 끈끈한 분비물과 닫히는 잎으로 '동물을 가둬요' ←정답

② produce bright flowers: 꽃을 피우는 기능이 아니에요

③ store extra rainwater: 빗물 저장은 문맥과 무관해요

④ reflect strong sunlight: 햇빛 반사는 포획 기관과 무관해요
det.tip: sticky secretions / closing leaves, that ______ → 동물을 가두다(trap animals).

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 모두 사용하여 (영어로) 쓰시오.

그 식물들은 자신에게 필요한 양분을 얻는다
[조건] (1) get, need, nutrition, plants, the, the, they 를 모두 사용 (2) 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '자신에게 필요한 양분'을 the nutrition (that) they need로, 관계사절을 활용해 영작해요.
det.analysis:
주어는 the plants(그 식물들)예요.

→ 동사는 현재형 get(얻는다)이에요.

→ 목적어 'the nutrition' 뒤에 목적격 관계대명사가 생략된 they need가 붙어 '그들에게 필요한 양분'이 돼요.

→ 완성: the plants get the nutrition they need
det.tip: the nutrition (that) they need = 그들에게 필요한 양분 (관계사절).

questions.wa: the plants get the nutrition they need
accept: the plants get the nutrition they need

questions.passage: They have also __________ (gain) enzymes that enable them to break down the food they consume and convert it into energy. As the enzymes work, they liquefy the prey’s body, releasing many of the nutrients that are absent from the soil.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: gain → gained: 'have also __________'는 현재완료라 과거분사 gained로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'They have also __________ enzymes'에서 'have + 과거분사'는 현재완료 시제예요. 식물이 효소를 '얻어 왔다(지금까지)'는 의미이니 gain을 과거분사 gained로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 gain을 gained로 써요.
det.tip: have + 과거분사 = have gained (현재완료).

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 모두 사용하여 (영어로) 쓰시오.

토양에 없는 양분
[조건] (1) absent, are, from, nutrients, soil, that, the 를 모두 사용 (2) 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '토양에 없는 양분'을 주격 관계대명사 that are를 활용해 영작해요.
det.analysis:
핵심 명사는 nutrients(양분)예요.

→ 뒤에 주격 관계대명사절 that are absent(없는)가 명사를 꾸며요.

→ '토양에'는 from the soil로 마무리해요.

→ 완성: nutrients that are absent from the soil
det.tip: nutrients that are absent from the soil (주격 관계대명사 that are).

questions.wa: nutrients that are absent from the soil
accept: nutrients that are absent from the soil

Due to the environmental factors, over many successive generations, these plants have evolved unique mechanisms, such as pitcher-like bodies filled with sticky secretions or closing leaves, that trap animals. questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오. (영어로)

[ acidic / elements / is / necessary / provide / soil / the / to / too ] (9단어)

det.korean: '너무 ~해서 …할 수 없다'를 「too + 형용사 + to부정사」 구문으로 배열해요.
det.analysis:
주어는 the soil(토양)이에요.

→ 'is too acidic'으로 '너무 산성이다'를 나타내요.

→ 뒤에 'to provide necessary elements'를 붙여 「too ~ to V(너무 ~해서 …할 수 없다)」 구문을 완성해요.

→ 완성: the soil is too acidic to provide necessary elements
det.tip: too + 형용사 + to V = 너무 ~해서 …못 하다.

questions.wa: the soil is too acidic to provide necessary elements
accept: the soil is too acidic to provide necessary elements

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 모두 사용하여 (영어로) 쓰시오.

태양 에너지를 이용해 스스로 양분을 만들다
[조건] (1) by, create, energy, nourishment, own, solar, their, using 를 모두 사용 (2) 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '~을 이용해'를 「by + 동명사(using)」로, '스스로의 양분'을 their own nourishment로 영작해요.
det.analysis:
동사는 create(만들다)예요.

→ 목적어는 their own nourishment(그들 자신의 양분)예요.

→ '태양 에너지를 이용해'는 「by + 동명사」 구조로 by using solar energy로 써요.

→ 완성: create their own nourishment by using solar energy
det.tip: by using ~ = ~을 이용해 (전치사 by + 동명사).

questions.wa: create their own nourishment by using solar energy
accept: create their own nourishment by using solar energy
